```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Lei_2026_meropenem"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18091113>

Lei and colleagues developed a two-compartment population PK model for
meropenem in septic adults and asked whether plasma 4-pyridoxic acid (PDA), an
endogenous substrate of the renal organic anion transporters OAT1 and OAT3,
explains clearance variability beyond Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance
(CLcr). In the final model PDA enters clearance as a piecewise-linear ("hockey
stick") term: no effect up to an estimated knot of 26.5 ng/mL, and a linear
decrease above it. The authors then used Monte Carlo simulation to map the
probability of target attainment (PTA) for six regimens across CLcr and PDA
strata (Figures 5 and 6). This vignette checks the packaged covariate
equations exactly, simulates the study regimens, and reproduces the PTA heat
map of Figure 5.

# Population

The PopPK model was fitted to 138 meropenem concentrations from the 28
patients who had intensive sampling, a subset of a 49-patient single-centre
ICU cohort (Peking University Third Hospital, January 2022 to December 2024)
used for the exposure-response analysis. Demographics are tabulated only for
the full cohort (Lei 2026 Table 1): median age 74 years (IQR 64-85), 63.3%
female, all Han Chinese, median BMI 21.5 kg/m^2, median APACHE II 17 and SOFA
7, and 83.7% pulmonary infection. Baseline renal status (KDIGO) was normal in
21 patients, acute kidney injury (AKI) without renal replacement in 21, and
continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in 7. Median Cockcroft-Gault CLcr
was 47.1 mL/min (IQR 32.8-80.8), serum albumin 31.0 g/L (IQR 29.1-34.8) and
baseline PDA 6.8 ng/mL (IQR 4.3-17.3). Patients received 0.5 g q12h (3),
1.0 g q8h (19) or 1.0 g q12h (27), all as 1-h infusions (Section 3.1).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Lei_2026_meropenem")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source; this table
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | 7.21 L/h | Table 2, final model, CL; Eq. 3 leading coefficient |
| `lvc` | 7.41 L | Table 2, final model, Vc; Eq. 4 |
| `lq` | 6.45 L/h | Table 2, final model, Q |
| `lvp` | 9.33 L | Table 2, final model, Vp |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.29 | Table 2, CL-CLcr; Eq. 3 exponent |
| `crcl_ref_cl` | 2.62 L/h (fixed) | Eq. 3 denominator; Section 3.2.3 (PopPK-cohort median CLcr) |
| `e_pyridoxic_acid_bl_cl` | -0.042 L/h per ng/mL | Table 2, CL-PDA; Eq. 3 |
| `lpyridoxic_acid_bl_hinge` | 26.5 ng/mL | Section 3.2.3 (PDA cutoff estimated as a structural parameter); Eq. 3 |
| `e_alb_vc` | -3.67 | Table 2, Vc-ALB; Eq. 4 exponent |
| `alb_ref_vc` | 31.4 g/L (fixed) | Eq. 4 denominator; Section 3.2.3 (PopPK-cohort median ALB) |
| `e_dis_arf_vc` | 2.02 | Table 2, Vc-GROUP; Eq. 4 (x2.02 AKI, x4.08 = 2.02^2 CRRT) |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.264^2 = 0.0697 | Table 2, IIV on CL 26.4% (see Assumptions) |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.227^2 = 0.0515 | Table 2, IIV on Vc 22.7% |
| `etalq` variance | 1.086^2 = 1.179 | Table 2, IIV on Q 108.6% |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.0578) = 0.240 | Table 2, residual error, proportional (variance; see Assumptions) |
| `addSd` | sqrt(0.105) = 0.324 mg/L | Table 2, residual error, additive (variance) |
| Two-compartment ODEs | n/a | Eqs. 1-2 |
| CL hinge in PDA | n/a | Eq. 3 |
| Vc power in ALB, renal-status factor | n/a | Eq. 4 |

# Structural verification

## Covariate equations

The individual clearance and central volume returned by the solver must equal
Eqs. 3 and 4 exactly. CLcr is supplied in mL/min (the canonical `CRCL` column)
and converted to the paper's L/h inside the model.

```{r check-covariates}
mod <- readModelDb("Lei_2026_meropenem")

grid <- expand.grid(
  CRCL = c(20, 2.62 * 1000 / 60, 100),
  PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL = c(5, 26.5, 50, 100),
  ALB = c(25, 31.4, 40),
  grp = c("normal", "AKI", "CRRT"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
grid$id <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
grid$DIS_ARF <- as.numeric(grid$grp != "normal")
grid$RRT_CRRT_STATUS <- as.numeric(grid$grp == "CRRT")

ev_cov <- grid |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, CRCL, PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, ALB,
                DIS_ARF, RRT_CRRT_STATUS)

# zeroRe() removes every eta, so each id is a typical subject; rxode2 warns
# that a multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the intent here.
cov_chk <- suppressWarnings(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_cov, returnType = "data.frame")
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl, vc) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(grid, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    clcr_lh = CRCL * 60 / 1000,
    cl_eq3 = ifelse(PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL <= 26.5,
                    7.21 * (clcr_lh / 2.62)^0.29 - 0.042 * 26.5,
                    7.21 * (clcr_lh / 2.62)^0.29 - 0.042 * PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL),
    vc_eq4 = 7.41 * (ALB / 31.4)^-3.67 *
      c(normal = 1, AKI = 2.02, CRRT = 4.08)[grp],
    cl_err = abs(cl / cl_eq3 - 1),
    vc_err = abs(vc / vc_eq4 - 1)
  )
stopifnot(nrow(cov_chk) == nrow(grid))

knitr::kable(
  cov_chk |>
    dplyr::filter(ALB == 31.4, grp == "normal") |>
    dplyr::select(CRCL, PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, cl, cl_eq3) |>
    dplyr::rename("CLcr (mL/min)" = CRCL, "PDA (ng/mL)" = PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL,
                  "CL solved (L/h)" = cl, "CL from Eq. 3 (L/h)" = cl_eq3),
  digits = c(1, 1, 4, 4),
  caption = "Typical clearance from the solver against Eq. 3 (ALB 31.4 g/L, normal renal function)."
)

knitr::kable(
  cov_chk |>
    dplyr::filter(CRCL == 20, PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL == 5) |>
    dplyr::select(ALB, grp, vc, vc_eq4) |>
    dplyr::rename("ALB (g/L)" = ALB, "Renal status" = grp,
                  "Vc solved (L)" = vc, "Vc from Eq. 4 (L)" = vc_eq4),
  digits = c(1, 0, 3, 3),
  caption = "Typical central volume from the solver against Eq. 4."
)

# Eq. 4 prints the CRRT factor rounded to 4.08; the model carries 2.02^2 =
# 4.0804, a 1e-4 relative difference. Everything else is exact.
stopifnot(
  max(cov_chk$cl_err) < 1e-10,
  max(cov_chk$vc_err) < 2e-4
)
```

At the reference subject (CLcr 2.62 L/h = 43.7 mL/min, PDA at or below the
knot) clearance is 7.21 - 0.042 x 26.5 = 6.10 L/h: the leading coefficient of
Eq. 3 is not itself the typical clearance, because the flat arm of the hinge
still subtracts the slope times the knot. Up to the knot PDA has no effect
(the 5 and 26.5 ng/mL rows are identical); above it each 10 ng/mL lowers
clearance by 0.42 L/h.

## Clearance across the covariate space

```{r fig-cl-surface}
cl_surface <- expand.grid(CRCL = c(15, 30, 60, 100, 150),
                          PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL = seq(0, 125, by = 2.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cl = 7.21 * (CRCL * 60 / 1000 / 2.62)^0.29 -
                  0.042 * pmax(PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, 26.5))

ggplot(cl_surface, aes(PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, cl, colour = factor(CRCL))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 26.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Baseline PDA (ng/mL)", y = "Typical clearance (L/h)",
       colour = "CLcr (mL/min)",
       title = "Eq. 3: meropenem clearance against PDA and CLcr",
       caption = "Dashed line: the estimated knot, 26.5 ng/mL.")
```

The PDA term is subtracted, not multiplied, so at very low CLcr and very high
PDA Eq. 3 approaches zero clearance (at CLcr 15 mL/min and the cohort's
maximum PDA of 121.3 ng/mL it is 0.19 L/h). Simulations below stay inside the
covariate range where clearance is positive.

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The cohort approximates Table 1: CLcr and
PDA are drawn log-normally from their reported medians and interquartile
ranges, albumin normally, and renal status in the 21:21:7 proportions of the
full cohort. CLcr is truncated to 15-150 mL/min and PDA to the observed
maximum of 121.3 ng/mL, which keeps every typical clearance positive.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() draws the covariates. It does not fix rxode2's eta draws across
# machines with different thread counts, so every assertion below is written
# on medians and robust quantiles.
set.seed(20261123)

n_arm <- 150
draw_cohort <- function(n) {
  grp <- sample(c("normal", "AKI", "CRRT"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(21, 21, 7))
  data.frame(
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n, log(47.1), log(80.8 / 32.8) / 1.349), 15), 150),
    PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL = pmin(rlnorm(n, log(6.8), log(17.3 / 4.3) / 1.349), 121.3),
    ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 31.0, (34.8 - 29.1) / 1.349), 20), 45),
    DIS_ARF = as.numeric(grp != "normal"),
    RRT_CRRT_STATUS = as.numeric(grp == "CRRT")
  )
}
cov_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  draw_cohort(n_arm) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "1 g q8h", ii = 8),
  draw_cohort(n_arm) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "1 g q12h", ii = 12)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

typical_cl <- 7.21 * (cov_df$CRCL * 60 / 1000 / 2.62)^0.29 -
  0.042 * pmax(cov_df$PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, 26.5)
stopifnot(all(typical_cl > 0))

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Covariate = c("CLcr (mL/min)", "PDA (ng/mL)", "ALB (g/L)"),
    `Simulated median (IQR)` = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)",
      c(median(cov_df$CRCL), median(cov_df$PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL), median(cov_df$ALB)),
      c(quantile(cov_df$CRCL, 0.25), quantile(cov_df$PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, 0.25),
        quantile(cov_df$ALB, 0.25)),
      c(quantile(cov_df$CRCL, 0.75), quantile(cov_df$PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL, 0.75),
        quantile(cov_df$ALB, 0.75))),
    `Table 1 median (IQR)` = c("47.1 (32.8-80.8)", "6.8 (4.3-17.3)", "31.0 (29.1-34.8)")
  ),
  caption = "Virtual-cohort covariates against Lei 2026 Table 1."
)

t_end <- 72
make_events <- function(row) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 1000, ii = row$ii, until = t_end - row$ii, dur = 1,
                   cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, t_end, by = 0.25), cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame()
  ev$id <- NULL
  ev$id <- row$id
  cbind(ev, row[rep(1, nrow(ev)), c("CRCL", "PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL", "ALB", "DIS_ARF",
                                     "RRT_CRRT_STATUS", "treatment")],
        row.names = NULL)
}
events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(cov_df, cov_df$id), make_events))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261123)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "treatment",
                       returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(nrow(sim) > 0, all(sim$cl > 0))
```

## Concentrations against time since the last dose (Figure 2)

Figure 2 plots the 138 observed concentrations against time since the last
dose. The panel below shows the simulated steady-state (day 3) envelope for
the two main study regimens, with the observed concentration range
(0.28-223.12 mg/L, Section 3.1) dashed.

```{r fig-tad}
ss <- sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(ii = ifelse(treatment == "1 g q8h", 8, 12)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_end - ii) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - (t_end - ii))

env <- ss |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc),
                   Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(env, aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.28, 223.12), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since last dose (h)", y = "Meropenem concentration (mg/L)",
       title = "Simulated steady-state 5th-50th-95th percentiles, 1-h infusions",
       caption = "Compare with Lei 2026 Figure 2. Dashed: observed range.")
```

```{r check-range}
# The 90% envelope must sit inside the observed range: a dose-unit or volume
# error would move it by an order of magnitude.
stopifnot(
  min(env$Q05) > 0.28 / 5,
  max(env$Q95) < 223.12,
  median(ss$Cc) > 1,
  median(ss$Cc) < 50
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the final dosing interval of each arm. The paper
reports no NCA table, so the reference is the identity that holds for linear
PK at steady state, AUC(0-tau) = Dose / CL, using each subject's own drawn
clearance.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- ss |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == max(time)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")

intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("1 g q8h", "1 g q12h"),
  start = c(t_end - 8, t_end - 12),
  end = t_end,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(nca_wide) == 2 * n_arm)

chk <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::inner_join(sim |> dplyr::distinct(id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_expected = 1000 / cl,
                pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / auc_expected - 1))

chk |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax = median(cmax), cmin = median(cmin), auclast = median(auclast),
    auc_expected = median(auc_expected),
    med_pct = median(pct_diff), q90_abs_pct = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Median Cmax,ss (mg/L)" = cmax,
                "Median Cmin,ss (mg/L)" = cmin,
                "Median AUC0-tau (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
                "Median Dose/CL (mg*h/L)" = auc_expected,
                "Median % difference" = med_pct,
                "90th pct |% difference|" = q90_abs_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA steady-state exposure against AUC(0-tau) = Dose/CL.")

# Both sides use the same drawn CL; the residual is trapezoid error on the
# post-infusion decay plus the approach to steady state of slow eliminators
# (CRRT subjects carry a fourfold Vc). Assert on the centre and a robust
# quantile, not on the extremes.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff)) < 3,
  quantile(abs(chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 10
)
```

# Reproducing the PTA heat map (Figure 5)

Figure 5 prints, for six regimens and seven (CLcr, PDA) strata, the PTA for
100% fT > MIC at nine MICs; Figure 6 (100% fT > 4xMIC) is the same grid
shifted by two MIC doublings. Since 100% fT > MIC means the steady-state
trough exceeds the MIC, one steady-state solve per stratum and regimen gives
every MIC. The paper does not discuss protein binding; meropenem is about 2%
bound, so the targets are applied to the total concentration `Cc` here.

Section 2.6 says the simulations incorporated "the parameter variability and
covariate distributions from the final PopPK model" but does not say how
albumin and renal status were set. Three readings are simulated: the
reference subject (ALB 31.4 g/L, normal renal function); albumin drawn from
Table 1 with normal renal function (the primary comparison); and both albumin
and renal status drawn from Table 1.

```{r pta-sim}

fig5_long <- fig5 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::starts_with("m"), names_to = "mic", values_to = "paper") |>
  dplyr::mutate(mic = as.numeric(sub("^m", "", mic)))

regs <- data.frame(reg = c("1g q12h 1h", "1g q12h 3h", "1g q12h 6h",
                           "1g q8h 1h", "1g q8h 3h", "2g q8h 3h"),
                   dose = c(1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 1000, 2000),
                   ii = c(12, 12, 12, 8, 8, 8),
                   tinf = c(1, 3, 6, 1, 3, 3))
strata <- unique(fig5[, c("crcl", "pda")])
mics <- sort(unique(fig5_long$mic))
n_pta <- 200
t_ss <- 168  # a multiple of 8 and 12; > 10 half-lives for every stratum

pta_variant <- function(variant) {
  set.seed(20261123)
  alb <- if (variant == "reference") rep(31.4, n_pta) else
    pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pta, 31.0, (34.8 - 29.1) / 1.349), 20), 45)
  grp <- if (variant == "ALB and renal status drawn")
    sample(0:2, n_pta, replace = TRUE, prob = c(21, 21, 7)) else rep(0, n_pta)
  subj <- merge(strata, data.frame(i = seq_len(n_pta), ALB = alb, grp = grp)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(),
                  DIS_ARF = as.numeric(grp >= 1),
                  RRT_CRRT_STATUS = as.numeric(grp == 2))
  res <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(regs)), function(r) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(amt = regs$dose[r], ii = regs$ii[r], until = t_ss - regs$ii[r],
                     dur = regs$tinf[r], cmt = "central") |>
      rxode2::et(t_ss, cmt = "central") |>
      as.data.frame()
    ev$id <- NULL
    full <- merge(ev, subj[, c("id", "crcl", "pda", "ALB", "DIS_ARF", "RRT_CRRT_STATUS")]) |>
      dplyr::mutate(CRCL = crcl, PYRIDOXIC_ACID_BL = pda) |>
      dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
    rxode2::rxSetSeed(4242)  # common random numbers across regimens
    tr <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, full, returnType = "data.frame")
    tr <- tr[tr$time == t_ss, c("id", "Cc")]
    tr <- merge(tr, subj[, c("id", "crcl", "pda")], by = "id")
    stopifnot(nrow(tr) == nrow(subj))
    expand.grid(mic = mics, k = seq_len(nrow(strata))) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        reg = regs$reg[r], crcl = strata$crcl[k], pda = strata$pda[k],
        model = mapply(function(m, cc, pp) 100 * mean(tr$Cc[tr$crcl == cc & tr$pda == pp] > m),
                       mic, crcl, pda)
      ) |>
      dplyr::select(-k)
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(res) |> dplyr::mutate(variant = variant)
}

variants <- c("reference", "ALB drawn", "ALB and renal status drawn")
pta <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(variants, pta_variant)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig5_long, by = c("reg", "crcl", "pda", "mic"))
stopifnot(nrow(pta) == 3 * 42 * 9)
```

```{r pta-compare}
pta <- pta |>
  dplyr::mutate(paper_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(paper)))
cmp <- pta |>
  dplyr::group_by(variant) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    checked_cells = sum(paper == "ok"),
    checked_reproduced = mean(model[paper == "ok"] >= 90),
    numeric_cells = sum(paper_num >= 5 & paper_num <= 95, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_diff = median((model - paper_num)[which(paper_num >= 5 & paper_num <= 95)]),
    median_abs_diff = median(abs(model - paper_num)[which(paper_num >= 5 & paper_num <= 95)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = variants)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(variant)

knitr::kable(
  cmp |>
    dplyr::rename("Simulation covariates" = variant,
                  "Cells marked >= 90%" = checked_cells,
                  "Fraction the model puts >= 90%" = checked_reproduced,
                  "Cells printed 5-95%" = numeric_cells,
                  "Median model - paper (points)" = median_diff,
                  "Median abs difference (points)" = median_abs_diff),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Packaged model against the 378 cells of Lei 2026 Figure 5."
)

primary <- cmp[cmp$variant == "ALB drawn", ]
# Realised: 98% of the checked cells reproduced; median gap about -3 points,
# median absolute gap about 4.5. The reference subject and the fully drawn
# cohort bracket the printed grid (about -7 and +9.5). A clearance or unit error
# (for example CLcr not converted from mL/min) shifts every cell by tens of
# points and fails these bounds.
stopifnot(
  primary$checked_reproduced > 0.9,
  abs(primary$median_diff) < 10,
  primary$median_abs_diff < 12,
  cmp$median_diff[cmp$variant == "reference"] <
    cmp$median_diff[cmp$variant == "ALB and renal status drawn"]
)
```

```{r pta-by-pda}

  dplyr::filter(variant == "ALB drawn", paper_num >= 5, paper_num <= 95) |>
  dplyr::group_by(pda) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cells = dplyr::n(), median_diff = median(model - paper_num),

  dplyr::rename("PDA (ng/mL)" = pda, "Cells printed 5-95%" = cells,
```

The primary reading reproduces the printed grid to a median of a few points,
and the two alternative readings bracket it. The PDA 100 ng/mL row is the
exception: there the model's PTA sits above the printed values in every
regimen, so the paper's own simulation evidently gave that stratum a higher
or more variable clearance than Eq. 3 implies. The PDA 25 and 50 ng/mL rows,
which carry most of the dosing recommendations, are reproduced closely.

## Values quoted in the Results

Section 3.5 quotes several PTAs to two decimals; the model's values under the
primary reading are listed beside them.

```{r pta-text}
quoted <- read.csv(text = "reg,crcl,pda,mic,paper
1g q12h 1h,30,100,2,94.48
1g q12h 1h,30,25,2,59.92
1g q12h 3h,30,50,2,84.28
1g q12h 3h,60,50,2,60.64
1g q12h 1h,60,25,1,61.92
1g q8h 1h,60,25,1,94.50
1g q8h 1h,60,25,2,77.92
1g q8h 3h,60,25,2,89.08
2g q8h 3h,30,25,8,84.58
1g q8h 3h,30,25,8,53.18")

quoted_cmp <- quoted |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    pta |> dplyr::filter(variant == "ALB drawn") |>
      dplyr::select(reg, crcl, pda, mic, model),
    by = c("reg", "crcl", "pda", "mic"))
stopifnot(nrow(quoted_cmp) == nrow(quoted))

knitr::kable(
  quoted_cmp |>
    dplyr::rename("Regimen" = reg, "CLcr (mL/min)" = crcl, "PDA (ng/mL)" = pda,
                  "MIC (mg/L)" = mic, "Paper PTA (%)" = paper, "Model PTA (%)" = model),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "PTAs quoted in Lei 2026 Section 3.5 against the packaged model."

stopifnot(median(abs(quoted_cmp$model - quoted_cmp$paper)) < 12)
```

The ordering claims of Section 3.5 all hold in the model: at CLcr 30 mL/min
the high-PDA stratum reaches a higher PTA than the low-PDA stratum, PTA falls
as CLcr rises, q8h beats q12h at the same daily dose, and extended infusion
helps at the higher MICs.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV is the SD of eta, not a CV.** Table 2 prints IIV as percentages
  (26.4% CL, 22.7% Vc, 108.6% Q). Section 3.2.3 quotes the CL and Vc
  variances as 0.052 and 0.069, which are 0.227^2 and 0.264^2 -- the squares
  of the two percentages, attached in the prose to the opposite parameters
  (Table 2 and the Abstract both give 26.4% for CL). The percentages are
  therefore read as sqrt(omega^2) and the variances as their squares; the
  alternative log(1 + CV^2) reading would give 0.0675 for CL, which matches
  neither quoted variance.
- **Residual error is printed as variances.** Table 2 lists the proportional
  and additive residual errors as 0.0578 and 0.105, the raw NONMEM SIGMA
  variances. The model uses their square roots, a 24.0% proportional SD and a
  0.324 mg/L additive SD. Read as SDs instead, the proportional error would be
  5.8%, which the observed-versus-IPRED panel of Supplementary Figure S1A
  rules out: several points between 30 and 80 mg/L lie 20-50% from the line
  of identity. Residual error does not affect any PTA above, which uses
  individual predictions as the paper does.
- **The renal-status covariate is split into two indicators.** The paper's
  GROUP covariate has three levels. It is encoded as `DIS_ARF` (1 for any
  acute kidney injury, including CRRT patients) and `RRT_CRRT_STATUS` (1 on
  CRRT), with the Vc factor `2.02^(DIS_ARF + RRT_CRRT_STATUS)`. Table 2
  reports a single estimated GROUP parameter of 2.02, and Eq. 4's CRRT
  factor of 4.08 is its square (2.02^2 = 4.0804), so one parameter carries
  both levels. The combination `DIS_ARF = 0`, `RRT_CRRT_STATUS = 1` is not a
  level of the source covariate.
- **CLcr units.** Eq. 3 uses CLcr in L/h centred at 2.62 L/h; the model takes
  the canonical Cockcroft-Gault column in mL/min (not BSA-normalised) and
  converts with `CRCL * 60 / 1000`. The 2.62 L/h centring value is the median
  of the 28-patient PopPK subset, which is not otherwise tabulated.
- **Clearance can reach zero.** Eq. 3 subtracts the PDA term, so typical
  clearance becomes non-positive when CLcr is very low and PDA very high
  (below about 13 mL/min at the cohort's maximum PDA). The model is encoded
  as published; the virtual cohort is truncated at CLcr 15 mL/min.
- **IIV multiplies the whole clearance.** Section 2.3 states exponential IIV;
  Eq. 3 gives only the typical value, so `exp(etalcl)` is applied to the full
  hinge expression, the usual NONMEM form `CL = TVCL * EXP(ETA(1))`.
- **Simulation covariates.** The paper does not state how albumin and renal
  status were set in its Monte Carlo simulations. Three readings are shown;
  the primary one (albumin drawn from Table 1, normal renal function) is the
  closest to Figure 5. Covariate distributions in the virtual cohorts are
  log-normal (CLcr, PDA) or normal (albumin) fitted to the Table 1 medians and
  IQRs, which come from the full 49-patient cohort rather than the 28-patient
  PopPK subset.
- **Figure 5 transcription.** The PTA grid was transcribed from the printed
  heat map; cells marked with a tick (PTA >= 90%) are recorded as such.
  Figure 6 was checked to be Figure 5 shifted by two MIC doublings, so it is
  not reproduced separately. The Section 3.5 statement that 1 g q8h over 3 h
  at CLcr 60 mL/min, MIC 0.5 mg/L "dropped below target in the low PDA group"
  matches Figure 6 (4xMIC, 89%), not Figure 5.
- **Not reproduced.** Figure 3 (individual fits for patient 1021) and Figure 4
  (pcVPC) need the observed data, which are not public. The exposure-response
  analysis (Section 3.4, Supplementary Table S3) is a set of univariable
  regressions on simulated exposure metrics, not a model, and is not part of
  this extraction.
- **Covariates screened but not retained.** Platelet count on Vc and 24-hour
  urine output on CL entered in forward selection and were removed in
  backward elimination (Supplementary Table S2); they are recorded in the
  model's `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Literature check.** No erratum or correction notice was found for the
  article as of November 2026.
